refraction_domain: Geometrical optics at a locally smooth interface between homogeneous isotropic stationary ordinary transparent media, with positive real phase indices evaluated at the same optical frequency.
v1 and v2 denote phase velocities, not group velocities. A stationary interface preserves frequency.
Angles theta1 and theta2 are measured from the interface normal, not from the surface.
The ordinary transmitted propagating ray is considered when it exists; anisotropic, moving, absorbing or negative-index media are not silently included.
lens_domain: Ideal centered thin lens, geometrical optics and first-order paraxial rays; aberrations and diffraction are neglected.
The same homogeneous isotropic surrounding medium lies on both sides. Thick-lens principal-plane offsets are neglected, so distances are measured from the common thin-lens plane/optical center.
The source notation is retained: d is object distance, f is image distance, F is focal length. Lowercase f is not renamed as focal length.
Finite conjugate-distance ratios require d and f nonzero and a finite image; collimated limits are identified separately.

source_real_positive_sign_convention.d_positive: Real object: incident rays diverge from an object point on the incident side of the lens.
source_real_positive_sign_convention.d_negative: Virtual object: incident rays already converge toward a point on the outgoing side where they would meet without this lens; their continued incident supporting lines define that point. This is explicitly present in SOURCE205, not an omission or a generic real-object-only restriction.
source_real_positive_sign_convention.f_positive: Real image: outgoing refracted rays actually converge to a point on the outgoing side.
source_real_positive_sign_convention.f_negative: Virtual image: backward extensions of outgoing diverging rays meet on the incident side.
source_real_positive_sign_convention.F_positive: Converging lens with real image-side principal focus.
source_real_positive_sign_convention.F_negative: Diverging lens with virtual image-side principal focus.
source_real_positive_sign_convention.coordinate_translation: Set the lens plane at x=0 and positive x along incident propagation. Then x_object=-d and x_image=f. These are not Cartesian signed coordinates substituted directly for d.
source_real_positive_sign_convention.unknown_distance_rule: An unknown d, f or F is solved as a signed variable in 1/d+1/f=1/F. The source instruction to write a plus sign before an unknown reciprocal does not force the computed unknown to be positive; a negative result identifies the corresponding virtual conjugate/focus.

magnification.source_size_ratio: \Gamma=H/h=|f|/|d|, with H and h nonnegative linear sizes and h>0.
magnification.signed_transverse_ratio: m=y_image/y_object=-f/d, with both transverse heights signed along the same transverse direction and y_object nonzero.
magnification.distinction: \Gamma=|m| is nonnegative and contains no orientation sign. m>0 means the same transverse orientation; m<0 means inverted orientation, including the consistent extrapolated conjugate description for virtual objects.
magnification.on_axis_size_caveat: A point on the axis has zero transverse height. Its literal H/h is 0/0 and is not used; local magnification may instead be defined by a nonzero infinitesimal transverse displacement.

independent_derivation: At a stationary interface the incident and transmitted waves have the same frequency. Continuity of phase along the interface equates their tangential wave-vector components.

For isotropic media k_j=n_j*omega/c. Thus k1*sin(theta1)=k2*sin(theta2), giving n1*sin(theta1)=n2*sin(theta2). Isotropy makes ray direction parallel to the wave-vector direction in the stated ordinary-media domain.

The transmitted ray therefore lies in the incident plane defined by the incident ray and the normal. The incoming and outgoing geometrical ray paths lie on opposite sides of that normal within the plane.
For nonzero incidence and an ordinary transmitted ray, sin(theta1)/sin(theta2)=n2/n1=v1/v2. At normal incidence both angles are zero; use the product equation, not the undefined literal 0/0 ratio.
assumptions: Use shared refraction_domain; no numerical medium or incidence angle is given.
The law describes transmission when a propagating refracted ray exists; beyond a critical angle in the higher-to-lower-index direction there is no such propagating ray.
For exactly normal incidence the incidence plane is not unique, but the ray stays on the normal.

correct_explanation_candidate.zh: 在静止、均匀、各向同性的普通透明介质分界面上，入射光线、折射光线和入射点的法线共面，入射和折射的几何光路分居法线两侧。入射角和折射角都从法线量起，满足 n1 sin(theta1)=n2 sin(theta2)。同一频率下，非零入射时 sin(theta1)/sin(theta2)=n21=n2/n1=v1/v2，其中 v 是相速度。正入射时两个角都为零，应使用乘积形式；它不要求计算 0/0。
correct_explanation_candidate.en: At a stationary boundary between homogeneous isotropic ordinary transparent media, the incident ray, refracted ray and normal are coplanar; the incident and transmitted geometrical paths lie on opposite sides of the normal. Measure both angles from the normal. Snell's law is n1 sin(theta1)=n2 sin(theta2). At the same frequency, for nonzero incidence, sin(theta1)/sin(theta2)=n21=n2/n1=v1/v2, where v is phase velocity. At normal incidence both angles vanish, so use the product form rather than a 0/0 ratio.

unresolved_source_specifics: Exact earlier author definition wording was not supplied or read; the candidate is explicitly conditional on the stated physical domain.

solutions.original_question: 2. 光的绝对折射率与相对折射率有什么区别？
independent_derivation: Define an absolute phase index relative to vacuum: n_j=c/v_j.
Divide the second medium's absolute index by the first: n2/n1=(c/v2)/(c/v1)=v1/v2.
Define n21 as the index of medium 2 relative to medium 1. It depends on the ordered pair, whereas each absolute index uses vacuum as its fixed reference. Reversing the pair gives n12=1/n21.
assumptions: All phase velocities and indices are evaluated at the same optical frequency in shared refraction_domain.
c is the vacuum light speed. Neither c/v_group nor a ratio at different frequencies is the index meant here.
No numerical indices or specific media appear in the question.

correct_explanation_candidate.zh: 绝对折射率以真空为参照：n=c/v，其中 v 是该介质中同一频率光的相速度。相对折射率比较两个介质：介质 2 对介质 1 的 n21=v1/v2=n2/n1。前者用固定的真空参照，后者取决于所比较介质的顺序；交换顺序便取倒数。
correct_explanation_candidate.en: The absolute refractive index uses vacuum as its reference: n=c/v, with v the phase velocity at the frequency considered. The index of medium 2 relative to medium 1 is n21=v1/v2=n2/n1 at that same frequency. Absolute index has a fixed vacuum reference; relative index compares an ordered pair of media and becomes its reciprocal when the order is reversed.

unresolved_source_specifics: The ordered notation n21 is explicitly defined here; no unprovided source notation or medium is inferred.

solutions.original_question: 3. 全反射的临界角等于什么？
independent_derivation: In the incident-medium-to-transmitted-medium direction, Snell's law requires sin(theta2)=(n1/n2)*sin(theta1).
The limiting propagating refracted ray has theta2=90 degrees from the normal. Therefore n1*sin(theta_c)=n2 and theta_c=arcsin(n2/n1).

A non-grazing critical angle and total internal reflection require n1>n2. For theta1>theta_c the required sin(theta2) would exceed one, so no propagating transmitted ray carries power away normally in the second medium.

For an ordinary lossless isolated interface this is total internal reflection. An evanescent field may still exist in medium 2. Equality theta1=theta_c is the limiting grazing-transmission condition, not an ordinary finite-angle transmitted ray.
assumptions: Shared refraction_domain, with lossless media and no nearby second interface producing frustrated total internal reflection.
Both angles are from the normal, and n1>n2 refers to the actual direction of incidence.
No numerical critical angle is determinable because no indices are supplied. If n1<=n2 there is no total-internal-reflection threshold for incidence below 90 degrees.

correct_explanation_candidate.zh: 光从折射率 n1 较大的介质射向折射率 n2 较小的介质时，才有普通全反射的临界角。折射角从法线量起达到 90 度时，入射角就是 theta_c，满足 sin(theta_c)=n2/n1，即 theta_c=arcsin(n2/n1)。入射角大于临界角时，在无损且不发生受抑全反射的界面上发生全反射；第二介质仍可有倏逝场。题目没有给出折射率，不能写出一个具体角度。
correct_explanation_candidate.en: For incidence from medium 1 into medium 2, total internal reflection requires n1>n2. The critical incidence angle is reached when the refracted angle, measured from the normal, is 90 degrees. Hence sin(theta_c)=n2/n1 and theta_c=arcsin(n2/n1). Incidence above this angle gives total internal reflection at a lossless interface without frustrated transmission, although an evanescent field can remain in medium 2. No numerical angle is specified by this question.

unresolved_source_specifics: The question supplies no medium pair or indices; none are invented.

solutions.original_question: 4. 什么样的透镜叫薄透镜？
independent_derivation: A real lens refracts at two separated surfaces. If the axial thickness is negligible compared with their relevant curvature radii, the inter-surface propagation and displacement of the effective refraction planes can be neglected to the intended accuracy.

In that thin-lens approximation the two surfaces are treated as one lens plane and the principal planes as coincident. When using distances from the optical center in the elementary formula, their offsets must also be negligible compared with the relevant conjugate and focal distances.
Thinness concerns neglect of thickness, not whether a lens converges or diverges. It does not by itself guarantee paraxial accuracy or remove aberrations.
assumptions: For spherical surfaces, the comparison is with the magnitudes of the finite surface radii; a plane surface has infinite radius.
The approximation is accuracy-dependent. No fixed millimeter cutoff, radius or diameter is given by the question.
The later formula and construction rules additionally need shared lens_domain; 'thin' alone is not a universal exact optical model.

correct_explanation_candidate.zh: 若透镜沿主轴方向的厚度与两表面的相关曲率半径相比很小，以至于在所需精度下可以忽略厚度和两个折射面的间隔，就可把它作为薄透镜。初等模型把它的有效折射作用集中在一个平面，并忽略主平面的分离；用光心量物距、像距时，这些偏移也须可忽略。薄透镜可以是会聚透镜，也可以是发散透镜；薄并不等于所有光线都严格符合近轴公式。
correct_explanation_candidate.en: A lens is treated as thin when its axial thickness is small compared with the relevant surface curvature radii, so that thickness and the separation of the refracting surfaces can be neglected at the required accuracy. The elementary model concentrates refraction in one plane and neglects principal-plane separation; those offsets must also be negligible when measuring conjugate distances from the optical center. A thin lens may converge or diverge. Thinness alone does not make nonparaxial imaging exact.

unresolved_source_specifics: The earlier author's exact thin-lens definition is not within the permitted prose. This is an independently stated approximation, not a recovered quotation.

independent_derivation: For paraxial incident rays parallel to the principal axis, a converging lens bends rays toward an axial intersection. A diverging lens produces divergent outgoing rays whose backward extensions meet at an axial point. That point is the image-side principal focus.
The object-side principal focus is the axial conjugate point for which incident rays have supporting lines through, or directed toward, that point and leave parallel to the principal axis.

With the same surrounding medium and a centered ideal thin lens, the two principal foci have equal distance magnitudes from the lens plane. With x positive along incidence they lie at x=-F (object-side focus) and x=F (image-side focus). For F<0 their virtual conjugate roles and physical sides reverse.
assumptions: Use shared lens_domain; 'parallel' means parallel to the principal axis, not an arbitrary off-axis parallel bundle.
The image-side focus is real for a converging lens and virtual for a diverging lens. Do not require outgoing divergent rays to meet physically.
The equal focal-distance magnitudes belong to the same-medium thin-lens model; they are not an assertion about every thick lens or unequal-medium system.

correct_explanation_candidate.zh: 与主光轴平行的近轴光线经透镜折射后，其光线会聚的轴上点，或发散光线反向延长线相交的轴上点，叫像方主焦点。会聚透镜的像方主焦点是实焦点，发散透镜的是虚焦点。物方主焦点则是使出射光成为平行于主轴的光束的轴上共轭点。理想薄透镜两侧为同一介质时，两个主焦点到透镜平面的距离大小相等；不能把虚焦点误说成出射光线实际会聚的位置。
correct_explanation_candidate.en: The image-side principal focus is the axial point where paraxial rays incident parallel to the principal axis converge after refraction, or where the backward extensions of divergent outgoing rays meet. It is real for a converging lens and virtual for a diverging lens. The object-side principal focus is the axial conjugate point that gives an outgoing bundle parallel to the axis. For an ideal thin lens in the same medium on both sides, the two focal-distance magnitudes are equal; virtual-focus rays do not physically converge there.

unresolved_source_specifics: The question does not itself specify a lens type. Both real and virtual principal-focus meanings are retained rather than inventing a particular lens.

independent_derivation: Let a signed object conjugate be at (-d,y_o), and let a ray cross the lens plane at height y. Its paraxial incident slope is theta_in=(y-y_o)/d. This remains valid for a virtual object, for which d<0 and the incident supporting lines converge toward x=-d>0.
An ideal thin lens of signed focal length F changes the slope by theta_out=theta_in-y/F. The sign is fixed by the image-side principal-focus definition.
At a proposed image plane x=f the ray height is y_i=y+f*theta_out=y*(1+f/d-f/F)-(f/d)*y_o.
For all rays from the same object conjugate to have the same image height, the coefficient of y must vanish. Hence 1/d+1/f=1/F, with y_i=-(f/d)*y_o.
If optical power D is used as in SOURCE204, D=1/F and the same equation is 1/d+1/f=D, with consistent reciprocal-distance units. No numerical D is given.
assumptions: Use shared lens_domain and the complete source_real_positive_sign_convention, including virtual objects.
d>0 for a real object and d<0 for a virtual object; f>0 for a real image and f<0 for a virtual image; F>0 for a converging lens and F<0 for a diverging lens.
These are signed optical distances, not three unsigned magnitudes and not interchangeable Cartesian coordinates.

For a real object at d=F the outgoing bundle is collimated: 1/f=0 in the infinite-image-distance limit; there is no finite image plane. Other collimated limits are treated through reciprocals, not division by zero.
An unknown reciprocal is written with the equation's plus sign and solved as signed; a negative result is not discarded.

correct_explanation_candidate.zh: 在薄透镜、近轴、两侧同介质的模型中，透镜公式为 1/d+1/f=1/F，也可写成 1/d+1/f=D，其中 d 是物距，f 是像距，F 才是焦距，D=1/F。沿用原文的实量取正规则：实物 d>0、虚物 d<0；实像 f>0、虚像 f<0；会聚透镜 F>0、发散透镜 F<0。虚物是入射会聚光束若没有本透镜便将在出射侧会聚的点。未知量须按有符号量求解，计算得负值表示相应的虚物、虚像或虚焦点，不能把未知量前的加号理解成结果一定为正。
correct_explanation_candidate.en: For a paraxial thin lens with the same surrounding medium on both sides, 1/d+1/f=1/F, or 1/d+1/f=D with D=1/F. Here d is object distance, f is image distance, and F is focal length. Use the source's real-positive convention: d>0 for a real object and d<0 for a virtual object; f>0 for a real image and f<0 for a virtual image; F>0 for a converging lens and F<0 for a diverging lens. A virtual object is the outgoing-side point toward which incident rays would converge without this lens. Solve unknowns as signed quantities; a plus sign before an unknown reciprocal does not force a positive result.

solutions.original_question: 7. 为了作出透镜的成像图，利用什么光线为宜？
independent_derivation: For a converging ideal thin lens, the principal-focus definition sends a ray parallel to the principal axis through the outgoing-side real principal focus.

Optical reversibility sends a ray whose incident supporting line goes through the incident-side principal focus into a ray parallel to the principal axis. For a virtual object, extend the incident supporting line as needed; do not invent a physical passage through a point outside the actual ray segment.
At the optical center y=0, the thin-lens paraxial slope change -y/F vanishes, so the central ray is undeviated in the same-medium thin-lens model.

Two distinct independent rays determine a finite image point by their outgoing intersection for a real image, or by backward extension for a virtual image. A third independent ray checks consistency; the three named rules are not three independent observations if their lines coincide.

For an on-axis object point the three standard selected rays can all degenerate to the principal axis. Use other distinct paraxial rays through different aperture heights, or an off-axis limiting construction; do not claim that coincident axial lines uniquely locate the image.
assumptions: Use shared lens_domain. The explicitly listed trio is for a converging lens, not a claim that the question specifies a particular lens.

For a diverging lens, a parallel incident ray leaves as if from its incident-side virtual image focus; an incident ray directed toward the outgoing-side object focus leaves parallel; the central rule is unchanged within the model.
At a focal conjugate the outgoing rays are parallel and give an image at infinity rather than a finite intersection.
No source diagram was viewed, reconstructed or produced. The task requests which rays are convenient, not an invented drawing for an unspecified object position.

correct_explanation_candidate.zh: 对理想会聚薄透镜，常选三类近轴光线：平行于主轴的光线，折射后经过像方主焦点；入射支撑直线经过物方主焦点的光线，折射后平行于主轴；通过光心的光线，在同介质薄透镜近似下方向不变。通常两条不同且独立的光线即可定位有限像，第三条可核对；实像用出射光线交点，虚像用反向延长线交点。轴上物点会使这三条标准线重合为主轴，须另取不同孔径高度的近轴光线，不能把重合线当成独立定位依据。发散透镜应使用相应的虚焦点及延长线规则。
correct_explanation_candidate.en: For an ideal converging thin lens, use three convenient paraxial rays: a ray parallel to the principal axis refracts through the image-side principal focus; a ray whose incident supporting line passes through the object-side principal focus leaves parallel to the axis; and a ray through the optical center is undeviated in the same-medium thin-lens approximation. Two distinct independent rays usually locate a finite image, and a third can check it. Intersect outgoing rays for a real image or their backward extensions for a virtual image. For an on-axis point the three standard rays can coincide with the axis, so use distinct rays at other aperture heights. A diverging lens uses the corresponding virtual-focus and extension rules.

unresolved_source_specifics: No lens type, object position or figure is specified in this printed question. The converging-lens rules and their diverging-lens qualification are stated independently, not inferred as a source case.

solutions.original_question: 8. 什么叫做透镜的放大率？
independent_derivation: A linear magnification compares corresponding image and object linear sizes, not areas, volumes or angular sizes. SOURCE205 defines Gamma=H/h; SOURCE206 retains H/h=|f|/|d| and Gamma=|f|/|d|.
Independently, the central ray through the lens origin has equal incident and outgoing slopes. With signed conjugate coordinates x_object=-d and x_image=f, y_o/(-d)=y_i/f, so m=y_i/y_o=-f/d.
Take absolute values for nonnegative sizes H=|y_i| and h=|y_o|>0. Then Gamma=H/h=|m|=|f|/|d|.
The sign of m, not Gamma, records transverse orientation. This statement also uses the signed conjugate description for a virtual object and does not assume every object is real.
assumptions: Use shared lens_domain and source_real_positive_sign_convention for finite nonzero conjugate distances.
H and h denote size magnitudes here. Signed transverse heights are separately named y_i and y_o to avoid changing the source's nonnegative Gamma.
h must be nonzero. A zero-height on-axis point does not define H/h directly; a differential transverse magnification may be defined by a limiting displacement.
The focal-to-infinite-image case has no finite transverse image size ratio. No numerical enlargement factor or orientation is supplied by this question.

correct_explanation_candidate.zh: 线放大率是像的线度与物体对应线度之比。按原文以 H、h 表示非负大小且 h>0，Gamma=H/h=|f|/|d|，所以 Gamma 非负，只表示大小倍率，不表示正立或倒立。若另用同一横向方向的有符号高度定义 m=y_i/y_o，则 m=-f/d，Gamma=|m|；m>0 表示同向，m<0 表示倒向。这里 f 是像距而 F 是焦距，二者不能混用。
correct_explanation_candidate.en: Linear magnification is the ratio of an image's linear size to the corresponding object's linear size. With the source's nonnegative sizes H and h, where h>0, Gamma=H/h=|f|/|d|. Gamma is nonnegative and reports size, not orientation. If signed transverse heights instead define m=y_i/y_o, then m=-f/d and Gamma=|m|: positive m means the same transverse orientation and negative m means inversion. Here f is image distance, whereas F is focal length.
